name: pycytominer
what: Python package for reproducible image-based profiling: collates single-cell feature tables from high-content assays with standardised QC (median/rank normalisation, CV-based outlier detection, plate-effect diagnostics, batch alignment). Nature Methods 2025 methods paper.
why_better: Old plan combines morphology features ad hoc with no standardised QC -> technical/batch features and artifacts flow unchecked into the NTI; pycytominer's collate pipeline flags and removes them before modelling -> reproducible, batch-controlled feature set feeding the NTI model.
evidence: unverified (methods paper; no benchmark numbers in abstract)
source_title: Reproducible image-based profiling with Pycytominer (Serrano et al., Nature Methods 22:677-680)
fit_small_data: high - pure tabular preprocessing, no learned components; works on any N
fit_onnx_cpu: high - no deep model, CPU tabular compute, no ONNX export needed
risk: Designed for multi-channel fixed assays (Cell Painting); needs adaptation to single-channel phase-contrast + fluorescence morphology tables and its own plate structure

name: CellPainTR
what: Transformer encoder with source-specific context tokens that learns Cell Painting representations robust to batch effects; generalises out-of-distribution to unseen datasets without fine-tuning.
why_better: Old plan trains the NTI on per-plate features that drift across plates/protocols -> NTI unstable on new imaging conditions; frozen CellPainTR as feature extractor removes plate-specific variance at representation level -> stable NTI across new plates/time points without retraining.
evidence: outperforms ComBat and Harmony on JUMP dataset; OOD evaluation on unseen Bray et al. dataset - qualitative claims, no numbers stated (unverified)
source_title: CellPainTR: Generalizable Representation Learning for Cross-Dataset Cell Painting Analysis (Caruzzo & Ye, arXiv:2509.06986)
fit_small_data: medium - encoder pre-trained at JUMP scale; with 70 images it can only be used frozen, not fine-tuned
fit_onnx_cpu: medium - ViT forward pass exportable to ONNX but heavier than tabular models on CPU
risk: Pre-trained on fixed, multi-channel Cell Painting; transfer to live single-channel phase-contrast neurite images is unverified and could encode irrelevant channel semantics

name: BMDExpress 2 (multi-model benchmark concentration)
what: EPA tool that computes benchmark concentrations (BC) from high-dimensional dose-response data by averaging across 8 dose-response models and 4 endpoints (up, down, both, overall) with model weights and confidence limits.
why_better: Plain 4PL fits are model-form sensitive (one misspecified curve biases potency) -> model-averaged BC over 8 models hedges model-form risk and reports model uncertainty -> more robust per-endpoint potency estimates than a single 4PL, which the old plan lacks entirely (it goes linear NTI -> small NN).
evidence: unverified (methods brief report; no benchmark numbers in abstract; 170 citations)
source_title: BMDExpress 2: enhanced transcriptomic dose-response analysis workflow (Phillips et al., Bioinformatics 35:1780-1782)
fit_small_data: high - curve fitting per endpoint across a few dose levels is exactly its use case
fit_onnx_cpu: high - classical curve fitting, CPU; Java implementation (invoke as subprocess or port fitting to Python)
risk: Java desktop tool; integration into an offline ONNX-based app means subprocess calls or re-implementing the 8-model fit in Python; transcriptomic-focused defaults must be re-pointed at morphology endpoints

name: Bayesian BMD with bridge-sampling marginal likelihoods
what: Systematic evaluation of five marginal-likelihood approximation methods (MLE-Schwarz, MCMC-Schwarz, Laplace, density estimation, bridge sampling) used by Bayesian BMD software (BBMD, ToxicR) across 8 models and 3 priors.
why_better: A naive Bayesian BC (the old plan's 'hierarchical Bayesian dose-response' idea) inherits bias from its ML approximation, changing posterior model weights and the BMD -> selecting bridge sampling, shown to have the smallest approximation and estimation bias, yields defensible Bayesian benchmark concentrations.
evidence: four real experimental datasets, 8 models, 3 priors; bridge sampling smallest bias regardless of dataset or prior - qualitative result, no single number (unverified)
source_title: Evaluating marginal likelihood approximations of dose-response relationship models in Bayesian benchmark dose methods for risk assessment (Minewaki et al., Comput Toxicol 2025, arXiv:2411.19066)
fit_small_data: high - MCMC/bridge sampling on 7-dose x 3-timepoint curves is cheap
fit_onnx_cpu: high - no deep model; CPU MCMC at fit time, results stored
risk: MCMC setup and convergence diagnostics cost expertise; with few replicates per well, posterior may be prior-dominated - must state priors explicitly in the app

name: deep-dose-response (hierarchical Bayesian end-to-end dose-response)
what: Hierarchical Bayesian model of dose-response curves across many compounds and cell lines with structured shrinkage sharing statistical strength across curves, fit end-to-end to high-throughput screening data; code public (PyMC).
why_better: Independent 4PL fits per (compound, timepoint) discard shared structure among the 3 time points and 2-3 compounds -> hierarchical shrinkage borrows strength across curves -> ~20% lower predictive error on held-out data and stable curves when wells-per-dose are few, directly addressing the 70-image constraint.
evidence: high-throughput cancer drug screening; ~20% lower predictive error on held-out data vs standard biology approach - as stated in abstract
source_title: Dose-response modeling in high-throughput cancer drug screenings: An end-to-end approach (Tansey et al., arXiv:1812.05691)
fit_small_data: medium - hierarchical priors are designed to help with sparse replicates, but prior hyperparameters were tuned at HTS scale and need re-tuning for a 3-4 compound study
fit_onnx_cpu: medium - PyMC/Stan sampling runs on CPU at this scale; fit-time only, no ONNX export, results cached in the desktop app
risk: Sampling time and prior-tuning effort; original code targets large compound x cell-line matrices, so adaptation to morphology endpoints is nontrivial

name: CGA2M+ (Explainable Boosting Machine with monotonicity and high-order terms)
what: Extends EBM (GA2M) with analyst-specified monotonicity constraints on selected features plus higher-order interaction terms; NeurIPS 2021.
why_better: Old plan's 'linear NTI then small NN' + post-hoc SHAP can emit non-monotone NTI-versus-dose artifacts and spurious interactions -> enforced monotonicity on dose (and time) makes the NTI biologically valid and the paper reports improved generalisation from the constraint -> cleaner dose-response NTI surface than the old plan's NN with SHAP-only XAI.
evidence: simulation + benchmark experiments; 'generalization performance improved by introducing monotonicity' - qualitative, no specific number (unverified)
source_title: Constrained Generalized Additive 2 Model with Consideration of High-Order Interactions (Watanabe et al., NeurIPS 2021, arXiv:2106.02836)
fit_small_data: high - glass-box boosting is competitive with neural nets on small tabular data and needs no GPU
fit_onnx_cpu: medium - EBM is a Python glass-box model; fast CPU scoring but no standard ONNX export (keep native scoring in the offline app)
risk: With only ~4-10 handcrafted morphology features, higher-order terms overfit; restrict to pairwise interactions; sign of monotonicity must be per-compound (H2O2/doxorubicin toxic vs curcumin protective)

name: Statistical inference for EBMs (shape-function CIs)
what: Boulevard regularisation makes EBM boosting converge to feature-wise kernel ridge regression, yielding asymptotically normal predictions, response prediction intervals, and confidence intervals for each learned univariate shape function; AISTATS 2026, code public.
why_better: SHAP-only XAI (old plan) gives effect magnitudes with no statistical uncertainty -> per-feature CIs let the team test whether each morphology parameter's NTI effect is significantly nonzero -> defensible 'which morphology drives NTI' claims instead of unstable SHAP rankings under 70-image noise.
evidence: minimax-optimal MSE O(p n^{-2/3}) for Lipschitz GAMs - theoretical guarantee; no dataset benchmark numbers (unverified)
source_title: Statistical Inference for Explainable Boosting Machines (Fang et al., AISTATS 2026, arXiv:2601.18857)
fit_small_data: medium - inference relies on asymptotics; marginal at ~200-500 cells total but adequate for well-aggregated morphology features
fit_onnx_cpu: medium - Python kernel-ridge computation on CPU, fit-time only; no ONNX
risk: AISTATS 2026 code is very new (possible bugs); asymptotic CIs can be anti-conservative at small N - validate coverage on simulated NTI data first

name: scam (shape-constrained GAM with smooth interactions)
what: R package scam for exponential-family GAMs with shape restrictions (monotonicity, convexity), recently extended to smooth interactions of covariates, linear functionals of shape-constrained smooths, and residual autocorrelation; arXiv 2024.
why_better: A vanilla GAM or the old plan's small NN can learn biologically implausible NTI-vs-dose shapes (e.g., recovery at high dose) -> monotone/convex constraints on dose and time shrink the hypothesis space -> more accurate, interpretable NTI curves at the 70-image sample size, beating an unconstrained NN.
evidence: unverified (methods/package paper; no benchmark numbers in abstract)
source_title: On some extensions of shape-constrained generalized additive modelling in R (Pya Arnqvist, arXiv:2403.09438)
fit_small_data: high - penalised smoothing with shape constraints is exactly the small-data regime
fit_onnx_cpu: high - classical R computation at fit time; export coefficient/shape tables to the app, no ONNX needed
risk: R dependency in a Python-centric app; constraint sign must be per-compound (forcing monotone-increasing NTI on curcumin, a protective control, would be wrong - check for hormesis at low H2O2 dose before constraining)

name: Integrated path stability selection
what: Stability-selection variant that integrates stability paths rather than maximising over them, giving much stronger upper bounds on expected number of false positives at the same target E(FP), at no extra compute; JASA 2025.
why_better: Plain stability selection (the sparse-linear-with-stability-selection idea) is so conservative it drops true morphology features -> tighter E(FP) bounds recover more true features at the same false-positive control -> a sparser yet more complete NTI feature set than vanilla subsampling-lasso.
evidence: simulations + two real cancer studies; 'significantly more true positives for the same target E(FP)' and 'no more computation than original' - qualitative, no single number (unverified)
source_title: Integrated path stability selection (Melikechi & Miller, arXiv:2403.15877)
fit_small_data: medium - subsampling-based; workable at ~100-500 rows but selection power is limited by N, and with only 4-10 features the exercise is near-moot unless the feature set is expanded
fit_onnx_cpu: high - resampled lasso fits, CPU, fit-time only
risk: Limited payoff with only a handful of morphology parameters; mainly useful if the feature set grows (e.g., to CellProfiler-scale features)

name: Conformal prediction methods for QSAR regression
what: Computationally efficient conformal prediction algorithms tailored to advanced ML models (deep neural networks, gradient boosting) for QSAR regression, producing valid prediction intervals under weak assumptions; validated on a collection of QSAR datasets plus simulations (2023).
why_better: Old plan reports point NTI values with no error bars for dose-response or hazard calls -> split conformal intervals give finite-sample coverage guarantees (e.g., 90%) around NTI predictions -> honest, distribution-free uncertainty without retraining the model.
evidence: validity and efficiency demonstrated on a diverse collection of QSAR datasets and simulations - no single number reported (unverified)
source_title: Development and Evaluation of Conformal Prediction Methods for QSAR (Xu, Liaw, Sheridan, Svetnik, arXiv:2304.00970)
fit_small_data: medium - needs an independent calibration split; with ~70 images hold out ~15-20 condition-cells for calibration
fit_onnx_cpu: high - post-hoc quantile computation on CPU, no model change
risk: Coverage guarantee requires exchangeability; plate/timepoint clustering violates it -> calibrate within strata (per timepoint/plate) or intervals will undercover

name: Mondrian (class-conditional) conformal prediction under class imbalance
what: Shows standard marginal conformal prediction hits its global coverage target while badly under-covering the minority class on imbalanced molecular datasets, and shows class-conditional (Mondrian) conformal prediction restores per-class coverage (NeurIPS 2025 workshop paper, 2026 preprint).
why_better: If NTI is binarised into toxic/non-toxic for a hazard call, marginal conformal can leave the rare toxic class nearly uncovered (realised minority coverage as low as 4.2% at a 90% target) -> Mondrian conformal restores per-class coverage at a modest prediction-set-size increase -> trustworthy hazard decisions on the minority class that the old plan has no uncertainty tool for.
evidence: four molecular datasets; realised minority coverage 64.8% (blood-brain-barrier penetration) and 4.2% (clinical-trial toxicity) under 90% marginal coverage; class-conditional conformal restores target coverage - as stated
source_title: A Quiet Failure in Calibrated Virtual Screening: Marginal Conformal Prediction Under-Covers the Minority Class, and a Class-Conditional Fix Recovers It (Tursunbadalov & Tursunbadalov, arXiv:2607.06605)
fit_small_data: medium - needs enough per-class calibration points; with few toxic-class examples use dose strata as the conditional axis instead
fit_onnx_cpu: high - post-hoc calibration, CPU, no retraining
risk: 2026 preprint with unverified code; per-class calibration sets can be tiny here, inflating interval widths

name: OECD-aligned in vitro DNT battery with BC + Pareto + ToxPi integration
what: 95 chemicals screened in an in vitro developmental-neurotoxicity battery covering key neurodevelopmental processes (proliferation, apoptosis, migration, neuronal differentiation, neurite outgrowth, maturation/synaptogenesis, oligodendrocyte differentiation, network formation) plus zebrafish behaviour; a benchmark-concentration pipeline with multi-objective Pareto optimisation and ToxPi radar scoring integrates the assays to rank DNT hazard (NIEHS/EPA/ToxPi team, Neurotoxicology 2026).
why_better: A single composite NTI scalar conflates potency and selectivity across endpoints -> BC per endpoint + Pareto front + ToxPi separates 'potent' from 'selective' effects and yields OECD-aligned DNT prioritisation -> more defensible, regulator-readable hazard ranking than an opaque NTI index, and it validates neurite outgrowth as a DNT-relevant endpoint.
evidence: 95 chemicals; neurite outgrowth assays and fungicides showed the highest percentage of selective hits; zebrafish assay most sensitive for potency - as stated in abstract
source_title: Prioritizing chemicals for developmental neurotoxicity by integrating data from a new approach methods (NAMs) battery covering key cellular events in neurodevelopment (Hall et al., Neurotoxicology 115:103485)
fit_small_data: high - a design and statistics framework (BC + Pareto + ToxPi), not a data-hungry model
fit_onnx_cpu: high - classical curve fitting and multi-objective ranking, CPU; no deep model
risk: Needs a well-estimated dose-response per endpoint and timepoint; with 7 doses x 3 timepoints the BC for weak endpoints will carry wide confidence limits, and curcumin (protective) complicates the standard 'toxicity increases with dose' framing

name: ARMED (adversarially-regularized mixed effects deep learning)
what: Non-intrusive framework adding to neural nets (1) an adversarial classifier forcing cluster-invariant features, (2) a random-effects subnetwork for cluster-specific effects, and (3) handling of unseen clusters; applied to live-cell image analysis among 4 applications.
why_better: Treating wells as i.i.d. in the old plan's NTI model ignores plate/well clustering and inflates significance of spurious plate effects -> separating cluster-invariant fixed effects from cluster-specific random effects -> up to 28% accuracy improvement on clustered data and honest generalisation to unseen plates.
evidence: 4 applications incl. live-cell image analysis; up to 28% accuracy improvement vs conventional models and up to 9% better generalization to unseen clusters - as stated
source_title: Adversarially-regularized mixed effects deep learning (ARMED) models for improved interpretability, performance, and generalization on clustered data (Nguyen & Montillo, arXiv:2202.11783)
fit_small_data: medium - adversarial + random-effects training is less stable with ~70 images; run the classical analogue (lme4/nlme linear mixed model on morphology features) first and only adopt ARMED if a neural NTI head is kept
fit_onnx_cpu: medium - neural net with extra subnetwork, ONNX-exportable but heavier than tabular models on CPU
risk: Adversarial training dynamics can fail to converge on small data; if the NTI model is a GAM/EBM (per other items), plain mixed-effects GLMM suffices and ARMED is unnecessary

name: Leakage-aware cluster split + applicability domain validation (ToxLens protocol)
what: Reproducible validation framework for molecular toxicity prediction: conservative curation, sphere-exclusion, leakage-aware UMAP-HDBSCAN cluster splits, temperature-scaled MC dropout with conformal-style prediction sets, and applicability-domain analysis; 11 ToxCast/Tox21 endpoints (2026 preprint).
why_better: Naive random k-folds leak related conditions/compounds into the test set, inflating NTI performance -> cluster-aware, leakage-controlled splits plus an applicability domain expose true out-of-domain performance -> the leave-one-compound-out / leave-one-dose-out validation numbers actually mean something when the index is reported.
evidence: 11 endpoints (Ames, acute oral, hERG, Tox21); five-seed soft-voting ensemble MCC 0.44, ROC-AUC 0.83, PR-AUC 0.58 on the leakage-controlled fold, exceeding four ECFP4 baselines on all 11 endpoints under the same split - as stated
source_title: ToxLens: A Reproducible Graph-Learning Framework for Leakage-Aware, Uncertainty-Calibrated Molecular Toxicity Prediction (Strømme et al., arXiv:2608.30472)
fit_small_data: medium - the split protocol transfers directly, but with only 2-3 test compounds 'compound-level' holdout is trivial; the valuable parts are cluster-aware well/plate splits and applicability-domain flags
fit_onnx_cpu: medium - the full framework is a graph-NN pipeline (heavy); for NTI adopt only the split logic and AD check, which are cheap CPU operations
risk: 2026 preprint, code unverified; molecular-scaffold machinery is irrelevant to a morphological study - adopt the validation logic, not the model
